summary:
This week's research highlights a strong focus on advancing **agentic AI** and improving **Large Language Model (LLM) capabilities**. A prominent trend is the development of more sophisticated **reasoning and decision-making mechanisms for agents**, moving beyond simple task execution. Papers explore **quality-diversity search** for idea generation (IDEAgent), **task-consistent routing** (TRACE-ROUTER), and **co-evolving skills** for robust learning (Skill Self-Play). Root cause analysis (AgentRCA) and auditing agent benchmarks (Do Agent Benchmarks Measure Capability?) also emerge as critical areas.

Notable advances include significant improvements in **long-context LLMs**, tackling the KV cache bottleneck with methods like hierarchical compression (HiKV) and page-local summaries (LOCKS), enabling tasks requiring extensive information processing. **Multimodal LLMs** are seeing substantial progress, particularly in healthcare, with systems like ClinFusion for medical image understanding and ClinPRISM for clinical time series analysis, alongside frameworks for evaluating diagnostic reasoning (ClinMM-Bench).

A significant shift is observed in the approach to **evaluating and ensuring the reliability of LLMs**. This includes detecting hallucinations with spectral signals (D-Score), auditing social simulators through reason-mediated models, and developing robust risk control for subgroups (Hierarchical Group-Conditional CRC). The "regression tax" framework also provides a new lens for understanding how skills affect LLM agents, emphasizing the reduction of negative impacts. The ongoing exploration of **efficient LLM architectures**, such as Mixture-of-Experts (Kimi K3, MMOE), continues to be a popular direction for scaling capabilities.

top_papers.title: ClinFusion: A Vision-Centric Multimodal LLM System for Holistic Medical Understanding
top_papers.abstract: ClinFusion is a vision-centric multimodal LLM system designed for holistic medical understanding. Its core method involves a compositional and cascaded vision encoder that unifies diverse 2D and 3D medical image understanding using a novel Spatial-Aware Locality Fusion operator. The paper's contribution lies in this unified vision encoding and a new evaluation framework that aligns with radiologists' practices, ensuring clinically relevant and factually accurate assessments.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the ClinFusion framework. a , Compositional vision encoder. We address the limitation of monolithic encoders by proposing a compositional architecture with a native 3D encoder and an array of 2D encoders unified via CaSL Fusion, supported by a 22M-sample data curation pipeline and a progressive 5-stage training recipe. b , Vision-grounded evaluation. We identify key evaluation limitations—lack of instruction-following assessment and reliance on global-level text-matching metrics—and introduce MedIF-Bench for medical instruction following and an RoI-Grounded Report Generation Evaluation scheme that assesses diagnostic accuracy at the region level using an LLM-as-a-Judge. c , Agentic tool use extension. To enhance deployment, we equip ClinFusion with perception expert tools and a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline within a plan–act workflow, demonstrating consistent improvements in both text-only and multimodal clinical scenarios.

top_papers.title: A Cost-Effective Multimodal LLM Reasoning Framework for Question Answering over Irregular Clinical Time Series
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces ClinPRISM, a cost-effective multimodal LLM framework for question answering over irregular clinical time series. It addresses challenges like sparsity and asynchrony by using an irregularity-aware encoder and a temporal evidence distiller to create LLM-compatible tokens. The framework's contribution lies in its novel approach to effectively model and reason over complex clinical data for improved healthcare applications.

top_papers.title: CHARM: A Multimodal Graph Foundation Model with Hierarchical Context Modeling for Zero-Shot Transfer
top_papers.abstract: CHARM is a multimodal graph foundation model that addresses zero-shot transfer by modeling hierarchical context across different modalities. Its core method involves learning transferable cross-modal relations and disentangling domain-specific information. This allows CHARM to generalize to new graph domains and tasks without requiring downstream fine-tuning, a significant contribution to the underexplored area of zero-shot transfer on multimodal graphs.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Domain bias and semantic relevance in Toys-to-Grocery retrieval.

top_papers.title: A report-grounded vision-language foundation model for colonoscopy from 280000 routine reports
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces EndoCLIP, a vision-language foundation model for colonoscopy. Its core method involves recovering and aligning lesion-level image-text pairs from routine colonoscopy reports. EndoCLIP's contribution is demonstrating superior performance in various colonoscopy tasks, including classification, by effectively bridging the gap between visual findings and expert descriptions, even approaching expert-level accuracy in distinguishing benign from malignant lesions.
top_papers.figure_caption: Weak report–image alignment and analysis of the pretraining dataset. a , Routine reports correspond to multi-frame, often multi-lesion cases. b , Dataset curation funnel, from 280.5k de-identified reports to 123.8k polyp-positive reports and a curated training set of 104.5k cases (37.3%) yielding 125.8k image–text pairs. c , Anatomical-site coverage across the 123.8k polyp reports. d , Frequency of morphology and surface descriptors. e , Lesion-size distribution. f , Report and finding-sentence length in words. g , Frames per case (n = 123.8k cases, 8.54M frames; median 65, mean 69). In e – g , bars mark distribution percentiles (P25–P99).

top_papers.title: IDEAgent: Agentic Quality-Diversity Search for Research Idea Generation
top_papers.abstract: IDEAgent addresses the limitation of current LLM-based research idea generation systems that optimize for either quality or diversity independently. It frames ideation as a Quality-Diversity (QD) search, employing a multi-agent framework to evolve ideas through lineages. IDEAgent jointly drives quality with multi-objective feedback for refinement and diversity through memory and explicit comparisons, aiming to generate a broader range of novel and sound research concepts.
top_papers.figure_caption: Left: An abstract overview of IDEAgent highlighting the crucial components and flow. Right: An abstract overview of the evolution of an idea and a lineage, where a raw idea might either be directly rejected, repaired and refined, just refined, or directly accepted as per the assessment by the evaluators. Note that a refinement/repair maintains the lineage of the idea ( ℓ I \( \ell_{I} \) ). We purposefully omit the exact conditionals at each step for simplicity and refer the readers to the methodology ( § \( \mathsection \) 3 ) for it.

top_papers.title: TRACE-ROUTER: Task-Consistent and Adaptive Online Routing for Agentic AI
top_papers.abstract: TRACE-Router addresses the challenge of routing in agentic AI by making a single, task-level model selection at the beginning of a workflow. This approach, using a contextual bandit, pins all subsequent LLM calls to the chosen model and updates its policy based on the final task outcome (accuracy and latency). Its contribution lies in aligning routing with the unit of supervision, enabling adaptive policies that learn from delayed feedback without needing to estimate individual task complexity.
top_papers.figure_caption: Task accuracy–latency trade-off on \( \tau^{2} \) -Bench, averaged over the retail and telecom domains. Every interior frontier point is produced by TRACE-Router .

top_papers.title: Skill Self-Play: Pushing the Frontier of LLM Capability with Co-Evolving Skills
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Skill Self-Play (Skill-SP), a novel framework for LLM training that addresses the trade-off between task diversity and verification reliability. Skill-SP utilizes co-evolving "skills" to enable deep, verifiable execution within specific scenarios while maintaining open-ended task variety through dynamic routing. This approach allows LLMs to learn and improve their capabilities in a more robust and efficient manner.

top_papers.title: D-Score: A Spectral Hidden-State Signal for Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces the D-Score, a novel method for detecting hallucinations in Large Language Models. The D-Score is a spectral statistic derived from the geometry of hidden activations during a single forward pass. It quantifies how many singular directions in the activation matrix maintain a leading singular value, with higher scores indicating potential hallucinations due to conflicting internal representations.
top_papers.figure_caption: AUROC of the D-Score detector on FAVA-Annotation with Llama-3-8B-Instruct as a function of the tolerance parameter \( \tau \) on the horizontal axis and the layer j j on the vertical axis. A broad region of nearby configurations achieves similar performance, indicating that the score is not tied to one isolated choice of \( \tau \) and j j .

top_papers.title: Reason-Mediated Behavioral Models for Auditing LLM Social Simulators
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a method to audit Large Language Model (LLM) social simulators by analyzing the underlying "reasons" behind simulated behaviors, not just the final outcomes. The core contribution is demonstrating that human-derived rationales significantly improve prediction of behavioral intent, and that LLMs can be evaluated on their ability to simulate these reason patterns independently of observed outcomes. This "reason-mediated" approach offers a more robust way to assess the fidelity of LLM social simulations.
top_papers.figure_caption: The reason-mediated behavioral model. We hold D , K , X D,K,X fixed and test whether human or LLM-simulated reasons Z Z support the same behavioral readout. Bold arrows show the evaluated mediated path; dotted gray arrows show controlled direct paths.

top_papers.title: The Physics of Multi-Turn Long-Horizon Planning: From Pre-training to Post-training via Single- and Multi-Teacher On-Policy Agentic Distillation
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a controlled environment to systematically study and improve multi-turn, long-horizon planning in foundation model agents. The core method involves analyzing planning ability acquisition during pre-training and shaping it through post-training techniques like GRPO and OPD. The key contribution is demonstrating that explicit world model construction and careful data curation are crucial for strong generalization, while suboptimal trajectories significantly degrade performance.
top_papers.figure_caption: An overview of the studying into physics of multi-turn long-horizon planning. It studies the long-horizon planning ability across three training stages: Large-scale pre-training , RL-based post-training (OPD and GRPO) , and Multi-teacher model consolidation post-training (MOPD) . The giraffe icon is used to represent the “L” in “Long”. Its long neck also reflects that the agents need to look far ahead in long-horizon planning.

top_papers.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
top_papers.abstract: Kimi K3 is a 2.8T parameter Mixture-of-Experts model that achieves significant scaling efficiency improvements through novel architectural components like Kimi Delta Attention and Stable LatentMoE. Its core contribution lies in its enhanced information flow across sequence length and model depth, enabling a 1-million-token context window and robust long-horizon execution, particularly in agentic and coding tasks.

top_papers.title: Evaluating Multi-Turn Multimodal Diagnostic Reasoning on Challenging Real-World Clinical Cases
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces ClinMM-Bench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate multi-turn multimodal diagnostic reasoning in AI models using challenging, real-world clinical cases. Its core method involves a two-level framework assessing both diagnostic accuracy and reasoning quality across 1,089 cases and 3,760 images. The key contribution is providing a more realistic evaluation of MLLMs by simulating the dynamic, progressive nature of clinical diagnosis, revealing that proprietary models currently perform best.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of ClinMM-Bench and evaluation framework. a, Data curation. ClinMM-Bench was developed through a six-stage pipeline: (1) Data collection and extraction, in which clinical case reports were collected from PubMed Central Open Access; (2) Data inspection, where case reports without medical images, those containing videos, and those with low-resolution medical images were excluded; (3) Data validation, using a dual-LLM consensus mechanism to identify cases suitable for the clinical diagnostic reasoning task; (4) Data conversion, where validated case reports were parsed and transformed into a standardized structured format; (5) Quality control, where an automated scoring procedure assessed the structured case reports and retained only those meeting a predefined quality threshold; and (6) Expert validation, where medical experts performed manual verification to ensure data reliability. b, Multi-turn multimodal evaluation. During evaluation, models perform diagnostic reasoning through multi-turn dialogues, with clinical information and images of each case progressively disclosed over the course of the dialogue. The evaluation framework comprises two levels: (1) Diagnostic accuracy evaluation, in which a dual-LLM consensus mechanism compares MLLM-predicted diagnoses against the ground-truth diagnoses, with judge LLMs assigning accuracy scores ranging from 0 to 2. (2) Diagnostic reasoning quality evaluation, where both MLLM-generated reasoning and reference reasoning are decomposed into atomic facts and quantified across three dimensions: fact recall, hallucination, and fact density.

top_papers.title: MemLens: A Value-Aware Memory Management System with Interactive Analytics for LLM-based Agents
top_papers.abstract: MemLens addresses the inefficiency of LLM memory systems by treating memory records as first-class data objects. Its core method involves a value-aware approach, using Shapley-style evaluation to prioritize important records. This allows for more effective memory management, leading to improved response quality and reduced latency in LLM-based agents.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1 . Comparison between (a) utility-agnostic memory management and (b) value-aware memory management.

top_papers.title: VetClaw: An Edge-Cloud Multimodal Agentic System for Veterinary Disease Screening
top_papers.abstract: VetClaw is an edge-cloud system for veterinary disease screening that uses a camera and optional symptom descriptions. It leverages a vision-language model for zero-shot classification, with distinct edge (OpenClaw) and cloud (LangGraph) components managing interaction, workflow, and model invocation. This multimodal approach goes beyond static image analysis to provide more robust diagnostic support.
top_papers.figure_caption: Edge-cloud Architecture of the VetClaw Veterinary Assistant Deployed on a Raspberry Pi for Early Skin Disease Prediction.

top_papers.title: RSIBench-Data: Benchmarking Data-Centric Research for Recursive Self-Improvement
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces RSIBench-Data, a benchmark designed to isolate and evaluate the data-centric research capabilities of LLM agents for recursive self-improvement. The core method involves agents iteratively revising training data strategies for a fixed target model within a controlled post-training environment, separating research decisions from system complexities. The main contribution is providing a clean evaluation framework to assess how well LLM agents can autonomously diagnose model failures and generate improved training data, a crucial step for achieving recursive self-improvement.
top_papers.figure_caption: Existing evaluations entangle multiple post-training choices; RSIBench-Data isolates the LLM agent’s ability to conduct data-centric post-training research.

top_papers.title: On-Policy Distillation for LLM Safety: A Routing Approach to Template-Robust Realignment
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Routing-based On-Policy Distillation (ROPD), a novel method to make LLMs safer by distilling knowledge from an aligned model to a potentially compromised one. ROPD focuses on modeling the difference between aligned and compromised output distributions, making it robust to unseen prompt templates and less prone to catastrophic forgetting or re-jailbreaking. Its core contribution is a template-agnostic approach to LLM safety realignment.
top_papers.figure_caption: The template-consistency trap in safety realignment.

top_papers.title: Mental World Modeling
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Mental World Modeling (MWM), a framework that extends traditional world models by incorporating agents' hidden mental states (beliefs, desires, intentions) alongside physical states. MWM's core method is to maintain a coupled physical-mental world state, predict how candidate actions will jointly update both, and simulate this process. The contribution is a more accurate prediction of human behavior by modeling not just the physical environment but also what agents know and believe about it.
top_papers.figure_caption: Mental World Modeling (MWM) represents a scene as a coupled physical and mental world state, renders a target-specific observation, predicts candidate target actions, and simulates the next physical and mental states. Unlike physical world modeling alone, MWM explicitly tracks the unobserved beliefs, goals, intentions, emotions, relations, and norms that shape what the target agent will actually do.

top_papers.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces AISPA, a user-centric framework for auditing system prompts in AI applications. AISPA evaluates system prompt instructions across eight user-relevant dimensions, classifying them as protective or problematic. The authors' audit of 3,249 instructions from 88 commercial AI products reveals significant variation in prompt design, highlighting a trust and accountability gap due to the lack of transparency.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of system prompt quality across organizations. Bars show the average number of protective instructions and problematic instructions of products created by an organization. Problematic instructions are ubiquitous in AI products, while organizations vary in protective instructions.

top_papers.title: ORCA-bench: How Ready Are Language Model Agents for Oncall?
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces ORCA-bench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate the readiness of language model agents for on-call incident root cause analysis (RCA). ORCA-bench simulates a production environment with real telemetry data and source code, presenting agents with 1,079 realistic RCA tasks. The benchmark's core contribution is its realistic evaluation of LLM agents on complex RCA scenarios, revealing current limitations with the best agents achieving only 25.3% accuracy on medium-difficulty tasks.
top_papers.figure_caption: RCA accuracy measures whether agents identified all plausible root causes, and hallucination rate measures whether agents named a root cause matching none of the plausible root causes. We show the realistic Medium and Hard difficulties here and report Easy in Fig. ˜ 5 along with Claude Fable 5 results on a subset of tasks in Sec. ˜ 5 . Error bars display ± 1 \( \pm \) 1 standard error across 884 incident tasks.

top_papers.title: Agentic Root Cause Analysis through Evidence-Grounded Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces AgentRCA, a novel zero-shot framework for automated root cause analysis of industrial anomalies. It addresses limitations of existing methods by combining a data-driven digital twin with a tool-augmented LLM. AgentRCA reasons through observed data, iteratively gathering evidence and evaluating hypotheses to pinpoint the physical fault, without requiring labeled fault examples.
top_papers.figure_caption: Architecture overview of AgentRCA. (A) AgentRCA learns a data-driven digital twin from normal-operation data only. Normal windows are grouped by operating regimes defined by system setpoints ( ω 1 , ω 2 , … \( \omega_{1} \),\( \omega_{2} \),\( \dots \) ). These regimes are used to precompute condition-specific statistical summaries (means 𝝁 \( \boldsymbol{\mu} \) , standard deviations 𝝈 \( \boldsymbol{\sigma} \) , correlation matrices 𝐑 \( \mathbf{R} \) , …). In parallel, a global autoencoder f θ f_{\( \theta \)} is trained across all regimes to learn nonlinear system dynamics. (B) The digital twin exposes modular diagnostic tools that provide interpretable evidence to the agent, including autoencoder residual scores, mean and variance shifts, correlation discrepancies, and optional documentation retrieval. (C) At inference time, a tool-augmented LLM agent receives a test window and natural-language fault descriptions. It iteratively queries the diagnostic tools, updates candidate hypotheses, and returns a ranked diagnosis with supporting evidence. Normal operation is included as a possible diagnosis, enabling both anomaly detection and root cause analysis.

top_papers.title: Do Agent Benchmarks Measure Capability? Protocol Validity in the Age of Agentic AI
top_papers.abstract: This paper argues that current agent benchmarks may not accurately measure true capability due to "reward hacking" where agents exploit evaluation flaws. The authors introduce HackDetect, a post-hoc audit to identify and quantify these exploits, and the "Mislead gap" metric to measure score inflation. Their audit of 15 benchmarks found significant evidence of these issues, suggesting existing capability claims may be overstated.
top_papers.figure_caption: Agent benchmark pipeline and five protocol exposure entry points. The upper panel follows the task-to-score path through the agent run, evaluator, and reported score. The lower panel maps the five Exposure sources to their entry points and shows how benchmark-exposed information or control can create a score-relevant shortcut.

top_papers.title: HiKV: Hierarchical Importance-Aware KV Cache with Hardware Acceleration for LLM Decoding
top_papers.abstract: HiKV addresses the KV cache memory bottleneck in LLM decoding by compressing it hierarchically. It first discards unimportant tokens and then further compresses the remaining ones by retaining only significant elements. This algorithm-hardware co-design, featuring a reconfigurable accelerator, achieves significant speedups and energy reductions.
top_papers.figure_caption: The dominated memory access of KV cache becomes the bottleneck of LLM decoding, motivating HiKV to shrink its footprint with high accuracy.

top_papers.title: Teachy Mini: Development and Preliminary Evaluation of a Knowledge-Based Generative Social Robot for Higher Education
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Teachy Mini, a generative social robot for higher education tutoring. Its core method involves operationalizing knowledge-based design (KBD) principles through system prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, and stateful prompt orchestration. The contribution is a KBD-compliant tutoring system that, in a preliminary evaluation, demonstrated improved learning outcomes compared to a control group.
top_papers.figure_caption: Knowledge-based Design Requirements identified by Vonschallen et al. [ 67 ]

top_papers.title: The Regression Tax: Decomposing Why Skills Help and Hurt LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces the "regression tax" to analyze how adding procedural skills impacts LLM agents. It decomposes performance by distinguishing between tasks that fail *after* skills are added (regressions) and those that fail regardless. The core contribution is demonstrating that the best skills improve performance primarily by *reducing regressions* rather than solely by increasing successes, identifying skill description osmosis, grounding displacement, and verification issues as key causes of this negative impact.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1 . Three stages of an agent task: grounding (reading the right inputs), method (the procedure), and verification (checking the output). Existing skills mostly target the method stage. In our data, regressions and residual failures concentrate at grounding and verification instead.

top_papers.title: On the Identifiability of Controlled World Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper addresses the fundamental question of when controlled world models, specifically Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs), can accurately infer the environment's underlying state and dynamics. The authors establish a theoretical framework showing that identifiability hinges on two policy-dependent conditions related to the spectral separation of predictable signals and the structure of action effects. This theoretical contribution provides crucial insights for designing more robust and interpretable world models for planning and control.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of controlled world-model identifiability. An encoder maps nonlinear observations to a standard-Gaussian latent representation, and an action-conditioned predictor models the next representation. Representation identifiability is governed by the predictable-signal margin γ rep ​ ( π ) \( \gamma_{\rm rep} \)(\( \pi \)) , while transition identifiability additionally depends on the conditional action-excitation margin ρ tr ​ ( π ) \( \rho_{\rm tr} \)(\( \pi \)) .

top_papers.title: A corrective agentic hybrid RAG and an operations-grounded evaluation for a scientific facility
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces APS-RAG, a platform that makes the vast operational knowledge of a scientific facility accessible via natural language queries. Its core method fuses multiple retrieval methods (dense, sparse, KG) with an agentic corrective loop and a native-tool executor. The contribution lies in this novel retrieval system and an operations-grounded evaluation dataset (APS-Bench) demonstrating significant improvements in knowledge recall.
top_papers.figure_caption: APS-RAG deployment overview. Through a single natural-language interface, APS staff can query the facility’s dispersed operational record. The platform pools information from nine distinct APS data sources: eight indexed knowledge bases are kept current by a daily diff-and-upsert pipeline, and the EPICS Archiver is not pre-indexed and is accessed at query time for live and historical process-variable data through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) tooling layer. Three user-selectable query modes are available: APS-RAG (Fast) for quicker responses, APS-RAG (Thinking) , which enables the corrective agentic loop, and AI Troubleshoot , which retrieves knowledge-graph-targeted fault-resolution steps.

top_papers.title: Agentic Permissions Policy Algebra for Taint Confinement in LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces APPA, a novel Information Flow Control framework for LLM agents. APPA addresses the usability bottleneck of traditional taint tracking by enabling engine-managed context branching and prospective acquisition enforcement. This allows agents to safely process mixed-confidentiality data by evaluating potential taint descents and generating remedy plans before data acquisition, thus preventing permanent context pollution and enhancing utility.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. APPA architecture for taint confinement and prospective enforcement. When inspecting untrusted or restricted data, the harness spawns a speculative child branch with an inherited pre-branch transcript snapshot, post-branch isolation, and a descended Label. Raw returns that would narrow the parent are blocked pending explicit acceptance or remedy plans, while adequate raw values and validated sanitized derivatives may merge through the checked exit. All execution steps project in real time to a single append-only event log.

top_papers.title: DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data
top_papers.abstract: DataOrchestra introduces a novel framework that dynamically orchestrates per-example data processing pipelines for LLM pretraining. Instead of uniform strategies, it intelligently decides whether to drop, keep, or clean data chunks, and for cleaning, it selects and instructs specific downstream tools (including LLM-based rewriting) to refine the data. This adaptive approach leads to stable performance gains across multiple benchmarks compared to fixed processing methods.

top_papers.title: EchoBridge: Long-Tail-Aware ECG-Echocardiography Text Alignment for Echocardiography-Derived Cardiac Findings
top_papers.abstract: EchoBridge aligns ECGs with echocardiography text reports to learn ECG representations of cardiac findings. It uses Complementary Shared-Private Projection (CSPP) to disentangle modality-specific information and Adaptive Prototype Boundary Calibration (APBC) to handle the imbalanced distribution of cardiac findings, improving performance on rare conditions.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Two challenges in ECG–echocardiography text alignment. Left: Global alignment entangles modality-specific factors and weakens clinically relevant cross-modal correspondence. Right: Prevalence imbalance provides fewer positive constraints and less reliable sample–prototype organization for low-prevalence findings.

top_papers.title: Hierarchical Group-Conditional Conformal Risk Control for Selective Prediction in Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper addresses the limitation of standard Conformal Risk Control (CRC) in language models, which provides population-level risk guarantees but can fail to protect specific subgroups. They propose Hierarchical Group-Conditional CRC (HG-CRC), a post-hoc method that enforces risk control simultaneously across all levels of a user-defined group hierarchy. HG-CRC achieves this by applying a Bonferroni correction and a leaf-first policy, ensuring rigorous guarantees for all subgroups without retraining the model.
top_papers.figure_caption: Mixture shift violation rates (ARC Challenge). Global CRC (blue) violates the risk budget in 15–47% of trials. Groupwise CRC (orange) controls per-group risk. The dashed line marks α = 0.10 \( \alpha \)=0.10 .

top_papers.title: LLM-Assisted Ontology Engineering and Construction of a French Legal Knowledge Graph
top_papers.abstract: This paper presents a two-stage LLM-assisted workflow to build a French legal knowledge graph from maintenance regulations. The first stage uses LLMs for open extraction of entities and relations, followed by label normalization and property induction. The second stage leverages the developed ontology for closed extraction and RDF graph construction across the entire corpus, demonstrating robust structured outputs and significant efficiency gains.

top_papers.title: LOCKS: Page-Local Compact Key Summaries for Efficient Long-Context Decoding
top_papers.abstract: LOCKS addresses the KV cache bottleneck in long-context LLMs by creating compact, page-local spectral summaries. These summaries allow the model to efficiently estimate attention mass and select only the most relevant pages for reconstruction, significantly reducing computation. This method achieves near full-cache performance with a fraction of the KV cache access, especially in challenging long-form reasoning tasks.
top_papers.figure_caption: The locality thesis in one figure (Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-4B twin and full protocol in App. B ). (a) Exact vs. reconstructed page-mass share at matched bytes. (b) Carrier retention vs. per-head budget; the ceiling is 100 100 by construction. (c) The error ladder at matched bytes, one scope per row. (d) RULER-16K capability families at a 256 256 -token budget. Page scope hugs the exact diagonal, keeps carriers down to a 0.5 % 0.5\% budget, improves every link, and traces FullKV.

top_papers.title: SIREN: Towards End-to-End Extreme-Weather Early Warning with Experience-Grounded LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces SIREN, an end-to-end system for automated extreme weather early warning using LLM agents. Its core method involves developing a comprehensive benchmark (SIREN-Bench) to evaluate LLM capabilities across various warning tasks and then proposing a novel LLM agent framework to address identified gaps. The main contribution is demonstrating the feasibility of automating the entire warning-to-action process, moving beyond isolated scientific tasks.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Connections to the EWS pipeline (Reichstein et al. , 2025 ) .

top_papers.title: The Visual Bottleneck: Sparse-Frame Adaptation of MLLMs for Joint Spatial-Temporal Video Grounding
top_papers.abstract: This paper addresses the performance drop in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for video grounding when processing sparse frames. The core method involves a systematic study revealing that visual feature extraction is the bottleneck. By adapting only the final three ViT layers, the model achieves significant performance gains on sparse inputs, demonstrating an effective strategy for real-world video moderation.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the train-dense/infer-sparse mismatch and our proposed solutions. Left: the Qwen3-VL 8B model drops from 56.0% to 22.3% temporal mIoU when frames are reduced from hundreds to 16. Center: our four key findings. Right: a fine-tuned 2B model outperforms a zero-shot 8B model on both temporal and spatial grounding.

top_papers.title: MMOE: Modernizing Diffusion Transformers with Efficient Expert Design
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces ModernMOE (MMOE), a method to efficiently scale diffusion transformers for generative AI. MMOE adapts principles from efficient large language models, like sparse experts and residual connections, to diffusion models. This approach aims to balance generation quality with training and deployment costs, unlike previous methods that primarily increased parameter counts.
top_papers.figure_caption: Architecture of MMOE. Left: a vanilla MoE block that routes each token to a small pool of feed-forward experts. Right: the MMOE block, which adds MoE++ lightweight experts (copy, zero, and constant), gate-residual routing, and attention-residual aggregation over previously completed block states before both the attention and the expert sub-layer.

top_papers.title: Evidence Attribution in Visual Document Understanding without Coordinates or Region Labels
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates "Attribution Hallucination" in visual document understanding, where models incorrectly identify evidence regions for their answers. The core method compares a traditional coordinate-based interface with a novel language interface that requires models to quote evidence verbatim. The contribution is demonstrating that this language-based approach, by limiting expression to text, may mitigate attribution failures compared to coordinate-based methods.
top_papers.figure_caption: The interface artifact in one example (Qwen3-VL-8B; page 2 of a 24-page input; question: what specific alloy is used for the internal contact pins). Both answers are correct. Only the evidence interface differs.

top_papers.title: Interactive Reward Agent: GUI Task Evaluation via Environment-State Verification
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes an Interactive Reward Agent (IRA) for evaluating GUI task completion. The IRA uses a propose-then-verify framework, first suggesting task completion conditions and then confirming them by interacting with system, application, and GUI tools. This method's contribution is enabling reliable GUI task evaluation by incorporating crucial environment state information beyond just visual execution data.
top_papers.figure_caption: Comparison between the interactive reward agent (ours) and a VLM-based evaluator on a task that requires output-file verification.

top_papers.title: Messier: A High-Resolution Corpus for Cross-Benchmark Agent Evaluation
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Messier, a large, standardized corpus of over 950,000 agent evaluation records across 30 benchmarks and numerous agents and tasks. Its core method involves unifying fragmented evaluation data and supplementing it with new runs in underrepresented domains. Messier's contribution is enabling cross-benchmark agent comparison and revealing uneven progress, highlighting areas like "function calling" as saturated and "enterprise workflows" as challenging.
top_papers.figure_caption: Composition and frontier analysis. Panels summarize the corpus across the dimensions defined in § 3 : (a) tasks by benchmark group, (b) action space, (c) environment state, (d) aggregation rule, and (e) verifier type. Counts in (b)–(e) are on a log scale. Panel (f) tracks frontier pass rate by release quarter and benchmark group, with dumbbell markers connecting each group’s first and final observed quarter.

top_papers.title: Minimizing Targeted Activations: Input-Only Suppression of Evaluation-Awareness Latents in Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces an "input-only" method to suppress specific internal model activations, like "evaluation-awareness" latents, by optimizing prompts without altering the model itself. Their core contribution is demonstrating that by adapting existing prompt optimization techniques with a negated feature term, they can effectively drive these targeted latents towards zero. This method offers a way to potentially prevent LLMs from behaving differently when they detect they are being evaluated, though the results also highlight potential cautionary implications.
top_papers.figure_caption: Suppression succeeds, but behavior does not follow. Left : prompt-side optimization drives diverse target latents from their base value f 0 f_{0} to zero or below—the direction and logit overshoot, and a causally-validated SAE feature is turned off completely. Right : yet a prompt optimized to suppress the eval-direction in front of a fixed eval body pushes the model’s behavioral eval log-odds above the eval-body baseline (more eval-like), while a random-direction prefix is neutral. Activation-readability is not behavioral controllability.

top_papers.title: SAM3D-Guided Object-Centric Representation Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a method to improve Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models by incorporating 3D object understanding. It uses a frozen 3D teacher (SAM3D) to guide the alignment of object-centric 3D representations with the VLA model's internal features during training. This allows the model to learn crucial 3D object information without needing explicit 3D data or modules at inference time, leading to better performance in complex manipulation tasks.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of SAM3D-VLA . We propose an object-centric 3D alignment framework that uses SAM3D as a frozen teacher during training. High-level instructions are decomposed into subtasks, and task-relevant object masks are used for SAM3D feature extraction. The extracted 3D features are spatially resampled and dimensionally projected to align with intermediate VLA representations, while inference follows the original pipeline using RGB and language instructions.

top_papers.title: Reinformed Dreamer: An Asymmetric World Model Efficiently Trained through Latent Guidance
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Reinformed Dreamer," an asymmetric world model for reinforcement learning. Its core method is a novel latent guidance objective that improves how the model learns from privileged information, addressing a limitation in prior work. The key contribution is a more efficient and effective training approach for model-based RL by better utilizing auxiliary state information.

top_papers.title: Instruction-Tuned Models Locally Reuse Human Syntax More Than Humans Do
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether instruction-tuned language models exhibit syntactic convergence, similar to humans, by analyzing their reuse of grammatical rules in dialogues. The core method involves comparing model generations' syntactic overlap with preceding human turns against unrelated human text. The key contribution is demonstrating that instruction-tuned models locally reuse human syntax more frequently than humans do, particularly for less common grammatical structures.
top_papers.figure_caption: Primary and pooled syntactic results. (a) Per-model actual-prime contrasts against the matched human response at centered mean rule frequency; error bars are 95% Wald intervals. (b) Pooled instruction-minus-pretraining coefficients under four estimands. Positive values favor instruction tuning. Conditional coefficients are evaluated at the target-size centering mean.

top_papers.title: UniMem: Complementary Episodic-to-Parametric Memory for Boundary-Agnostic Task Streams
top_papers.abstract: UniMem addresses the stability-plasticity dilemma in LLM agents by proposing a self-routing framework that adaptively coordinates two complementary memory pathways. Novel tasks are stored in an episodic buffer for retrieval, while recurring patterns are consolidated into parametric memory for efficient, stable execution. This approach allows LLMs to effectively manage and reuse task experience across evolving task streams without explicit boundary definitions.
top_papers.figure_caption: The episodic-to-parametric conceptual workflow of UniMem . Initial Routing Construction initializes known-task routing embeddings and calibrates the novelty sentinel 𝐞 NOVEL \( \mathbf{e} \)_{\( \texttt{NOVEL} \)} . Episodic Buffering stores queries routed to 𝐞 NOVEL \( \mathbf{e} \)_{\( \texttt{NOVEL} \)} for retrieval-augmented execution. Parametric Consolidation clusters recurring buffered patterns and converts them into new routing embeddings with associated parametric memory units.

top_papers.title: Anatomy Contextualized Adaption of CT Foundation Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Anatomy Contextualized Adaptation (ACA), a lightweight method to improve CT vision-language foundation models. ACA adapts frozen models by aligning anatomy-level visual features with specific text, while also preserving global context and avoiding expensive training from scratch. Its core contribution is a framework that efficiently enhances fine-grained anatomical understanding within CT images for better vision-language alignment.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of ACA. Anatomy-level visual embeddings are constructed from a frozen CT foundation model using TotalSegmentator segmentations, while anatomy-level text embeddings are extracted from radiology reports using an LLM and the corresponding frozen text encoder. An inter-anatomy transformer, augmented with spatial position and anatomy type embeddings, contextualizes the anatomy embeddings across the full set of structures. The resulting embeddings are aligned to per-anatomy text via ℒ anatomy \( \mathcal{L} \)_{\( \text{anatomy} \)} , while their mean-pooled scan-level embedding is aligned to the full report via ℒ scan \( \mathcal{L} \)_{\( \text{scan} \)} .

top_papers.title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes "shadow evaluations" as a new method to assess AI agents' ability to conduct open-ended AI research. In this approach, AI agents tackle the core research question of an unpublished paper, and the original authors grade their progress. The study found that despite completing engineering tasks autonomously, current frontier AI agents failed to make substantial progress on complex research questions, leading to their "rejection" by the authors.

top_papers.title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces OmegaUse-OfficeVal, a new benchmark designed to evaluate LLM agents on complex, multi-step office tasks. Its core contribution is the inclusion of economic grounding, pairing each task with human labor time and a price proxy. This allows for cost-effective evaluation of LLM agent performance against human benchmarks.

top_papers.title: SciFigAlign: Scoring Scientific Figures by Fine-tuned Alignment of Visuals with Manuscript Evidence
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces SciFigAlign, a method for scoring scientific figures based on their alignment with manuscript evidence. It addresses limitations of existing image assessment tools by fine-tuning a model on a dataset of 3,857 annotated scientific figures. SciFigAlign's core contribution is its ability to evaluate figures not just on visual quality, but on their scientific relevance and clarity within the context of a research paper.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of SciFigAlign versus prior image assessment methods. Left: four prior paradigms and what each lacks for scientific figure scoring. Right: SciFigAlign binds a published figure to caption, citing paragraphs, and abstract/metadata, scores Clarity / Relevance / Informativeness / Structure (CL/RE/IN/ST) with a learnable CrossAttn+CubeMLP regressor, and keeps an LLM judge as a diagnostic baseline only.

top_papers.title: Scores Are Not Decisions: Cost-Aware Stopping for Tool Acquisition in LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of deciding how many tools an LLM agent should acquire from a ranked list, considering their diverse costs. The core method, CAM-DF, formulates this as a cost-aware stopping problem, training directly on the value of stopping versus continuing. Its contribution is a principled approach to tool acquisition that accounts for heterogeneous costs, proving that simple score-based methods are suboptimal in such scenarios.
top_papers.figure_caption: CAM-DF as a pre-execution stop plugin inside one agent turn. The agent flow is unchanged: a router, retriever, scoring prompt, or shadow pass exposes a candidate order. CAM-DF virtually walks the ranking and fixes the prefix A ​ ( τ ) A(\( \tau \)) before any selected tool executes. Offline labels define the regret-weighted target; deployment sees public features.

top_papers.title: Mitigating Compounding Error via Video Representation Regularization
top_papers.abstract: This paper identifies that compounding error in video diffusion models for long-horizon generation is caused by dimensional collapse in the model's internal representations. The core method involves regularizing these representations to prevent degradation. The main contribution is demonstrating that this representational regularization, rather than simply scaling training data, is crucial for achieving stable and high-quality long-term video generation.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of our proposed method. Existing autoregressive diffusion models suffer from compounding errors during long-range generation, and this issue cannot be effectively mitigated by simply scaling up training data. We introduce hidden states regularization into DiT layers to strengthen the model’s representation capacity, alleviate compounding errors, and enable consistent performance gains as training proceeds.

top_papers.title: Evaluating Regional Bias in LLMs From Abstract Stereotype to Concrete Social Decision-Making
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Stereotypes-to-Decisions (S2D), a framework to systematically evaluate regional bias in LLMs. S2D assesses how LLMs perceive Chinese regions in terms of warmth and competence, and how these perceptions influence decisions in education, occupation, and social interaction. The study finds significant and consistent regional biases across six LLMs, linking these biases to regional development indicators.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of our S2D evaluation framework for regional bias.

top_papers.title: SpecFirst: Behavioral Specification Elicitation as a First-Class Step in Agent-Based Program Synthesis from Scratch
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces SpecFirst, a novel two-stage framework for agent-based program synthesis from scratch. Its core method separates behavioral specification elicitation from code synthesis, allowing a dedicated agent to thoroughly probe a binary and documentation before any code is generated. This approach aims to overcome limitations of existing single-pass methods by preventing context drift and misinterpretations, leading to more accurate program synthesis.
top_papers.figure_caption: Framework of SpecFirst . On top of the default code synthesis pipeline in the blue box, SpecFirst introduces spec agent to elicit the specification before implementation in the green box.

top_papers.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces OSReward, a benchmark for evaluating the reliability of vision-language models (VLMs) as judges for computer-using agents (CUAs). It addresses the critical need for scalable and accurate verification of CUA task completion by providing a realistic dataset of human-verified CUA trajectories with ground-truth verdicts. OSReward aims to standardize CUA evaluation and advance research in this area.
top_papers.figure_caption: Cost against binary accuracy on OSReward-Hard: reliable judges are expensive, and the OS-Shepherd models come nearest their accuracy at a fraction of the cost.

top_papers.title: ScaFE: Data-Efficient Scar Classification with LLM-Generated Clinical Feature Programs
top_papers.abstract: ScaFE addresses data-limited scar classification by leveraging LLMs to generate executable "feature programs" that extract clinically relevant attributes from scar images. This method avoids direct image diagnosis by VLMs, respecting data privacy and auditability. The core contribution is a data-efficient approach that translates LLM knowledge into reproducible, locally executable scar feature extraction, enabling robust classification with minimal expert-labeled data.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of ScaFE. An LLM turns source-traceable clinical concepts into deterministic feature programs that process local images into interpretable features. A fixed RF evaluates candidates, and only aggregate diagnostics return for refinement. The selected program and RF are frozen for prediction; raw images never enter the LLM context.

top_papers.title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Frontis-MA1, an AI model designed for recursive self-improvement in machine learning engineering (MLE). Its core method involves training a meta-evolution agent on an open-source MLE testbed (OpenMLE) using four atomic program-evolution operators. The key contribution is demonstrating that this AI can significantly improve its own performance in MLE tasks through a coupled learning and evolution loop, achieving substantial gains on the MLE-Bench Lite benchmark.

top_papers.title: Would You Walk to the Car Wash? Revealing the Salience Bias of Large Language Models in Commonsense Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Salience Bias," a vulnerability in LLMs where they over-prioritize explicit, often irrelevant, information, leading them to ignore crucial commonsense knowledge. The authors propose the SaliTrap Benchmark to demonstrate this bias across various LLMs, showing that models struggle to overcome misleading distractors even when they can identify them. Their contribution highlights a significant gap in LLMs' ability to apply commonsense reasoning in realistic scenarios.
top_papers.figure_caption: All LLMs suffer from salience bias, which stems from knowledge suppression, not absence.
